title: The Creator Margin, episode 12: Why your first price is too low

highlights.text: Here is the uncomfortable truth. Most creators price from fear, not from value. They pick the number that feels safe to say out loud. When I started, I charged two hundred dollars for a launch video that made my client forty thousand in a week. The video was not the problem. My price was. Nobody pays you for your hours. They pay you for the result.

I use a simple three-number test before every proposal. Write down your floor, the price where you would walk away. Then your target, the price that is fair for the result. Then your stretch, the price that makes you a little nervous. Now quote the stretch number first. Half the time the client says yes, and you just learned what you are actually worth.

Give them ninety days of notice and lead with what changed for them. Last year I told every client that our new rate starts in April, and I listed the results we delivered since the last increase. Out of eleven clients, ten stayed. The one who left was the one I was losing money on anyway. A price increase is not an apology. It is a progress report.
